subject: humanities
passage: The churches of Ravenna, a city on Italy's Adriatic coast, hold the finest surviving mosaics of the sixth century, a time when the city served as a center of Byzantine power in the West. The craftsmen worked with several kinds of tesserae: cubes of colored glass, whose surfaces were often set at slight angles so that they would catch light from different ______ pieces of marble and limestone, used for faces and hands; and gold tesserae, made by sealing a sheet of gold leaf between two layers of glass. Seen by lamplight, the gold backgrounds seem to shift and glow as the viewer moves.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The colon introduces a list of three kinds of tesserae, and each item contains commas of its own ("cubes of colored glass, whose surfaces …" and "pieces of marble and limestone, used for faces and hands"). When list items contain commas, semicolons separate the items, as the semicolon after "hands" shows. The same mark is needed after the first item.
explanation.A: Incorrect. A comma would blur the boundary between the first item and the second, since the items already contain commas; the semicolon after "hands" shows the separator the list uses.
explanation.B: Correct. A semicolon separates the first item of the list from the second, matching the semicolon before "and gold tesserae."
explanation.C: Incorrect. With no punctuation, the first and second items run together, and "different directions pieces of marble" cannot be read clearly.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A colon has already introduced the list; a second colon inside it is wrong, and "different directions" is not an independent clause.
